sourcedFrom: Beretta 90 Series Operators Manual — UD6A0537 REV 0002 (form code printed on the page; the book prints no year) (UNDATED — Beretta prints a form code rather than a year in these books)
cleanIntro: The 92's strip is one lever and four parts, and Beretta asks for it every time the pistol is fired or at least once a month. Work over a table: the recoil spring and guide come out under tension and are the parts that go on the floor.

steps.title: Unloaded first — and the manual will not let you skip it
steps.action: Every disassembly instruction in this book opens with the same demand: prove the pistol is unloaded. Magazine out, slide back, chamber looked at and felt. Do it before the disassembly lever is touched, because the lever will rotate on a loaded gun exactly as it does on an empty one.
steps.quote: FIELD STRIPPING CAUTION: MAKE SURE THE PISTOL IS UNLOADED. IF NOT, UNLOAD FOLLOWING THE “UNLOADING THE PISTOL“ PROCEDURE. (P. 22)
steps.cite: Beretta 90 Series Operators Manual — UD6A0537 REV 0002 (form code printed on the page; the book prints no year) — DISASSEMBLY — FIELD STRIPPING, printed p.26-27

steps.title: Magazine out, then the disassembly lever clockwise to its stop
steps.action: Drop the magazine, hold the pistol in your right hand, press the disassembly lever release button with your left forefinger and rotate the lever clockwise with your thumb until it stops. It goes to a hard stop — if it is only part way round the slide will not come off, and forcing the slide against a half-turned lever is how the lever gets bent.
steps.quote: Remove magazine by depressing magazine release catch. Hold pistol in the right hand; with left forefinger press disassembly lever release button and with left thumb rotate the disassembly lever clockwise until it stops.
steps.cite: Beretta 90 Series Operators Manual — UD6A0537 REV 0002 (form code printed on the page; the book prints no year) — DISASSEMBLY — FIELD STRIPPING, printed p.26-27

steps.title: Slide assembly forward off the frame
steps.action: With the lever at its stop, run the slide assembly straight forward off the frame rails. Barrel, locking block, recoil spring and guide all come with it — the slide is stripped on the bench, not on the frame.
steps.cite: Beretta 90 Series Operators Manual — UD6A0537 REV 0002 (form code printed on the page; the book prints no year) — DISASSEMBLY — FIELD STRIPPING, printed p.26-27

steps.title: ⛔ Recoil spring and guide are under tension — ease them out
steps.action: Press the recoil spring and its guide slightly toward the muzzle to free them from the barrel, then lift the guide and let the spring extend SLOWLY. This is the step that puts a spring across the room, and Beretta sets it in capitals on the page.
steps.aside: Lift spring guide and recoil spring, letting the spring out slowly, as it is under tension.
steps.quote: CAUTION: RECOIL SPRING AND RECOIL SPRING GUIDE ARE UNDER TENSION.
steps.cite: Beretta 90 Series Operators Manual — UD6A0537 REV 0002 (form code printed on the page; the book prints no year) — DISASSEMBLY — FIELD STRIPPING, printed p.26-27

steps.title: Barrel and locking block out — field strip complete
steps.action: Lift the barrel with its locking block assembly out of the slide. That is the whole strip: frame, slide, barrel and locking block, recoil spring and guide, magazine. Beretta stops the owner here in as many words.
steps.aside: NO FURTHER DISASSEMBLY IS RECOMMENDED UNLESS DONE BY A QUALIFIED GUNSMITH.
steps.quote: Remove the barrel and locking block assembly from slide.
steps.cite: Beretta 90 Series Operators Manual — UD6A0537 REV 0002 (form code printed on the page; the book prints no year) — DISASSEMBLY — FIELD STRIPPING, printed p.26-27

steps.title: Barrel from the chamber end, and the lug area gets oil after
steps.action: Solvent and a brush from the chamber end, then dry with patches, repeating until the barrel is clean. Then wipe the outside of the locking block and lug assembly with a solvent patch, let it dry, and oil the lug and locking block area — that is the surface doing the work in a falling locking block pistol.
steps.aside:
Wipe down exterior of barrel locking block and lug assembly with a
solvent soaked patch, allow to dry, then apply lubrication in the lug and locking block area.
steps.quote: Clean the barrel with bore solvent and a brush and then dry it with cleaning patches. Always begin at the chamber end.
steps.cite: Beretta 90 Series Operators Manual — UD6A0537 REV 0002 (form code printed on the page; the book prints no year) — MAINTENANCE, printed p.39-41

steps.title: Breech face, magazine lips and follower
steps.action: Brush the fouling out of the breech, the magazine lips, the follower and the receiver. A 92 that stops feeding is usually a dirty magazine rather than a dirty gun, and this is where that gets fixed.
steps.aside: Thoroughly clean the breechface with a brush and cloth to remove powder residue and debris.
steps.quote: Remove fouling from the breech, magazine lips, follower, and receiver with a brush and a cloth.
steps.cite: Beretta 90 Series Operators Manual — UD6A0537 REV 0002 (form code printed on the page; the book prints no year) — MAINTENANCE, printed p.39-41

steps.title: A thin coat everywhere, two drops on the main spring
steps.action: Apply a thin coat of oil to all the metal parts, check the firing pin assembly is sitting correctly, and put two drops of gun oil on the main spring. Thin is the operative word: excess oil in the bore is the hazard Beretta puts in capitals, and oil on a cartridge can kill a primer.
steps.aside: Apply 2 drops of gun oil to the main spring.
steps.quote: Apply a thin coat of oil to all metal parts.
steps.cite: Beretta 90 Series Operators Manual — UD6A0537 REV 0002 (form code printed on the page; the book prints no year) — MAINTENANCE, printed p.39-41

steps.title: Backstrap grip: this book names your frame
steps.action: If you want the grip panels off for a deep clean, this book's grip section is scoped by name to the Vertec-framed pistols — the 92X line, M9A3 and the M9A4 line. A 2 mm Allen wrench takes the grip screws counter-clockwise; mind the lock washers under them.
steps.aside: With a 2MM Allen wrench, remove the grip screws by turning them counterclockwise. Be careful not to lose the lock washers beneath the grip screws.
steps.quote: Applies to Vertec-framed models: 92X line, M9A3, M9A4 line
steps.cite: Beretta 90 Series Operators Manual — UD6A0537 REV 0002 (form code printed on the page; the book prints no year) — GRIP INSTALLATION, printed p.29

deepAbsentReason: Beretta publishes nothing past the field strip for an owner of a 90-series pistol and says so twice: "NO FURTHER DISASSEMBLY IS RECOMMENDED UNLESS DONE BY A QUALIFIED GUNSMITH" at the end of the strip, and "THE FIREARM SHOULD NOT BE DISASSEMBLED FOR CLEANING BEYOND WHAT IS DESCRIBED. ONLY ARMORERS OR OTHER HIGHLY-TRAINED PERSONNEL WHO ARE FAMILIAR WITH THESE FIREARMS SHOULD CONDUCT FURTHER DISASSEMBLY" in maintenance. A manufacturer's published DON'T outranks every other source, so nothing deeper is authored from anywhere else.

cleaning.name: BARREL
tasks: Brush in from the CHAMBER end and all the way through before pulling back
Solvent first if it needs it, then patches until one comes out clean
⛔ Never clean the barrel with the pistol assembled
Light oil on the whole barrel before it goes back

cleaning.name: SLIDE & BREECH FACE
tasks: Cloth or nylon brush on the breech face, extractor, rails and locking shoulders
Dry the slide surfaces, then lightly oil the guides

cleaning.name: RECOIL SPRING ASSEMBLY
tasks: Light gun oil on the spring guide assembly
Nylon brush first if it is heavily fouled — never a steel one

cleaning.name: FRAME & MAGAZINE
tasks: Fouling off the frame rails and the magazine well
Magazine lips and follower cleaned, then wiped with a lightly oiled rag
⛔ Never spray or apply oil to cartridges

reassembly: Engage the safety before anything goes together.
Barrel and locking block into the slide, extractor resting in its groove in the barrel; the barrel should sit perfectly flush.
Recoil spring onto its guide, then the guide head lodged in the centre of its groove in the locking block.
Slide assembly onto the frame rails and pushed back to or beyond the rear of the frame.
⛔ Rotate the disassembly lever back ONLY with the slide closed and aligned — that is Beretta's own instruction.
Make sure the barrel locking assembly is in its rear-most position; push it back through the slide opening if it is not.
Cycle the slide, decock, and function check before any ammunition.
fncheck: Reassembled and unloaded: rack the slide several times and confirm it returns fully into battery. Check the safety/decocking lever operates and, on an FS pistol, that it blocks the trigger. Beretta's own reassembly checks are worth repeating — the recoil spring guide head should sit in the centre of its groove in the locking block, the barrel should rest flush against the slide with the extractor in its groove, and the disassembly lever should only be rotated with the slide closed. If the slide does not close fully, stop and re-check the locking block before firing.
